text: CRD (Chronic Respiratory Disease) is primarily caused by the bacterium Mycoplasma, which spreads rapidly chicken-to-chicken but most commonly via the trans-ovarian route — eggs are contaminated in the layer's genital tract, infecting the chick before hatching. Symptoms range from wetness around the eye to swelling around the eye with open-mouth breathing and gurgling throat sounds; Mycoplasma damage to the respiratory tract opens the door for other infections (E. coli, Coryza, IB) to develop easily. Necropsy finding: air sacculitis — air sacs lose their normal thin, transparent look, showing mucus in mild cases or cheesy material/pus in severe secondary-infected cases. Treatment: Doxycycline and Tylosin are effective antibiotics against Mycoplasma; Doxycycline is often combined with Colistin to also cover secondary E. coli infection. Tylosin must be used for day-old chicks (DOC) — mixing Tylosin into drinking water from the day chicks arrive, for 5 days, destroys Mycoplasma passed from the layer and prevents CRD spreading through the farm.
